Hi all,

I?m trying to simulate a hypothetical network of 1000 nodes with three ergm terms: edges, absdiff(?age?), and gwesp(0.5). I tried a few target statistics and find it very hard to match the absdiff(?age?). Even I first simulate a network without this term, and then use the value of absdiff(?age?) of that network to be the target statistics, it still tells me ?Unable to match target stats? once I add the absdiff(?age?) term. Are there any tricks to make the target statistics to simulate a hypothetical network?

Thank you very much.

Best,
Lin

messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] Simulate a hypothetical network with target statistics
messages.body_plain:
Hi Lin -

On 5/15/2018 8:15 AM, Zhu, Lin wrote:
> I?m trying to simulate a hypothetical network of 1000 nodes with three 
> ergm terms: edges, absdiff(?age?), and gwesp(0.5). I tried a few 
> target statistics and find it very hard to match the absdiff(?age?). 
> Even I first simulate a network without this term, and then use the 
> value of absdiff(?age?) of that network to be the target statistics, 
> it still tells me ?Unable to match target stats? once I add the 
> absdiff(?age?) term. Are there any tricks to make the target 
> statistics to simulate a hypothetical network?

I was intrigued by your questions so just wrote code to give it a try 
myself. (You caught me over morning coffee when I had just enough 
time!)? It seemed to work perfectly on my end.? I'm using the latest 
ergm (3.8.0).? My code is here, followed by a few thoughts:

library(ergm)
mynet <- network.initialize(100, directed=FALSE)
mynet <- set.vertex.attribute(mynet, "age", sample(1:80,100,replace=TRUE))
mynet %v% 'age'
myergm1 <- ergm(mynet~edges, target.stats=200)
mynet <- simulate(myergm1)
myformula <- mynet~edges+absdiff("age")+gwesp(0.5, fixed=TRUE)
mystats <- summary(myformula)
myergm2 <- ergm(myformula, target.stats=mystats)
mynet <- simulate(myergm2)
mystats
summary(myformula)

- The "unable to match target stats" sometimes appears as a warning, not 
an error, letting you know as a courtesy that the algorithm cannot get 
the target stats exactly matched in the initial network.? This is 
especially true when your target stats are not integers but any 
individual network can only have integer values for those target stats. 
However, this is actually not a problem since the estimation algorithm 
used when supplying target stats is able to work just fine, even if the 
starting network for estimation is not exactly on the target stats.? 
That's why it is a warning only, not an error.? I expected this to be 
what I saw when I tried recreating your example. However, I didn't even 
get this warning.? Is this showing up for you as a warning or an error?? 
Is the estimation algorithm proceeding after it gives you the message?

- Are you trying to get the final simulated network to match the target 
statistics exactly?? That is not likely to happen, by design.? Each 
individual network simulated from an ergm is a stochastic process - they 
will only match the target statistics on average over many simulations.? 
If you need to match an exact set of target statistics in a single 
network, you can try using the san command; however this typically only 
works on relatively simple models.? Actually getting an individual 
network to be guaranteed to match a set of target stats for arbitrarily 
complex model is a difficult (impossible?) problem.

- If my code doesn't help you answer your question, can you send me 
yours so I can take a look?

Cheers, Steve

messages.body_plain:
Dear Golshid,

In ergm you do not set the lambda but the alpha (in prior versions it said
alpha instead of decay). And lamba is > 1 for every alpha > 0.
See Snijders et al 2006
<http://journals.sagepub.com/doi/abs/10.1111/j.1467-9531.2006.00176.x>,
p.113.


Best Regards,

messages.subject: [statnet_help] gof for valued networks
messages.body_plain:
Hi all, 

I have developed several ERGMs for a sparse network of food sharing in Alaska. The edges in the networks are currently being analyzed as binary but I do also have weighted edges indicating the number of resources exchanged between two nodes. I?ve been able to implement the same ERGMs for this valued network using the ergm.count extensions. The results are promising but the downside is that the goodness of fit tests do not exist for valued networks. 

Are there any updates on this issue? I am peripherally interested in developing them myself, assuming I have extra time after finishing my thesis, but the ideal would be to connect with someone that has developed these tools already or has begun to do. 

If anyone has any working code that begins to implement gof() with ergm.count, let me know! 

Best, 
Shane A. Scaggs 

Sent from Mail for Windows 10

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Interactions of GWESP with other ERGM terms
messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] Interactions of GWESP with other ERGM terms
messages.body_plain:
Dear Statnet Community,

Does it make sense to consider interactions between GWESP and other model terms? Imagine an instance with friendship data where we could hypothesize that the scaling parameter was different for different race/ethnicities, and the coefficient itself might vary by race/ethnicity. This is not precisely the case I am working on, but it seems like a close analogy that makes sense conceptually.

I have not seen an interaction term as described above, and I am asking for your thoughts on whether this would make sense.

Many thanks for your consideration.
Aditya

messages.subject: [statnet_help] gof for valued networks
messages.body_plain:
Hi, Shane,
On Mon, 2018-05-21 at 21:41 -0700, Shane A. Scaggs wrote:
> Hi all, 
>  
> I have developed several ERGMs for a sparse network of food sharing
> in Alaska. The edges in the networks are currently being analyzed as
> binary but I do also have weighted edges indicating the number of
> resources exchanged between two nodes. I?ve been able to implement
> the same ERGMs for this valued network using the ergm.count
> extensions. The results are promising but the downside is that the
> goodness of fit tests do not exist for valued networks. 

Glad it's useful!
>  
> Are there any updates on this issue? I am peripherally interested in
> developing them myself, assuming I have extra time after finishing my
> thesis, but the ideal would be to connect with someone that has
> developed these tools already or has begun to do. 
They are an open problem, though I believe that people in Carter Butt's
group might be working on it.
As a first-order diagnostic, it might be worthwhile to see how well the
model predicts the distribution of tie values. Here's a sketch of how
one might do it (using the Zachary dataset example):
library(ergm.count)example(zach)
# Simulate from the model fit along with the empirical CDF (the
atmost()s):zach.sim1 <-
simulate(zach.fit1,monitor=~atmost(0)+atmost(1)+atmost(2)+atmost(3)+atm
ost(4)+atmost(5)+atmost(6)+atmost(7), response="contexts",
nsim=1000,statsonly=TRUE)# Get the observed values, including for the
CDF:zach.obs1 <- summary(update(zach.fit1$formula,
.~.+atmost(0)+atmost(1)+atmost(2)+atmost(3)+atmost(4)+atmost(5)+atmost(
6)+atmost(7)), response="contexts")
# Plot and mark the observed value:boxplot(zach.sim1)points(zach.obs1,
pch=4, col=2)
The first half of boxplots are basically a convergence diagnostic. The
second half (the atmost()s)) give some indication of how well the count
distribution is being fit.
						I hope this helps,	
					Pavel
